subject: Proposed SLA addendum & fallback policy for regional burst windows (pilot)
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <claire@novamed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pilot SLA addendum for regional burst protection

Hi Mina / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the pilot for Novamed's clinician-assist feature, our compliance and platform teams have asked for a narrowly scoped addendum to the MSA that covers:

- guaranteed regional throughput windows during scheduled pilot hours (PST 08:00-20:00)
- a burst protection tolerance for short traffic spikes without breach credits (we proposed 10% of baseline for up to 2 hours/day)
- a defined "downtime grace period" before credits kick in for multi-region failover scenarios
- evidence types we can expect for a credit investigation (audit logs, call traces, deployment event timeline)

I've attached a short request packet that includes our expected traffic profile and a sample order form. We're not asking for a full custom SLA yet — this would be an addendum scoped to the 90-day pilot.

Can your team propose language we can run by procurement/legal? Also need to know if this impacts the order form pricing for Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: Novamed_SLA_Request.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Claire Donovan
Director, Platform Partnerships
Novamed Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pilot SLA addendum for regional burst protection

Claire — thanks for the packet and clear asks. Looping in Karthik (infrastructure / availability) and Michael (account lead) so we can turn around suggested addendum language and the commercial impact.

Immediate plan: 1) Karthik will draft the operational clauses (uptime %, burst tolerance window, grace period definition, evidence checklist). 2) Michael will confirm pricing/order form delta for Dedicated pilot capacity. 3) I will collate those into a single redline you can take to procurement/legal.

One quick question — for the burst tolerance you mentioned "10% of baseline for up to 2 hours/day." Is that a peak above the 95th percentile baseline, or above provisioned Dedicated throughput? If you can confirm a baseline number (rps or token/sec) that helps us give concrete thresholds.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Claire Donovan <claire@novamed.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pilot SLA addendum for regional burst protection

Thanks — technical notes below; attaching a proposed clause set (Redwood_proposed_sla_clauses_v1.docx).

Proposed operational clauses (draft):
- Uptime commitment (pilot scope, single-region primary with regional failover): 99.9% monthly availability during pilot business hours (PST 08:00-20:00). This is scoped to API ingress and token/response generation latency below the thresholds defined below.
- Latency SLOs (95th pct): 50ms per token for short responses (<128 tokens); 120ms per token for long-form (>128 tokens). These are measured at the route level as seen from the assigned Dedicated pool.
- Burst tolerance: allow up to 15% above provisioned throughput for no-credit tolerance for up to 3 hours/day during pilot hours. Bursts beyond this will be subject to normal credit rules. Rationale: small pilots can have noisy traffic; extra headroom reduces false positives.
- Downtime grace period: for regional failover events, a 30-minute grace window starts when the primary region detects sustained error rates >10% for 5 consecutive minutes. Credits apply only if the failover/resolution extends beyond the grace window.
- Credits schedule (pilot): 5% monthly service credit for a single pilot window breach; 15% cap per month. Evidence request: audit logs (request ids + timestamps), KV cache eviction logs (if applicable), deployment timeline, and routing decision records.

Notes / alternatives:
- If Novamed needs a shorter grace window (e.g., 10 minutes), latency-sensitive workflows may require additional Dedicated headroom or cross-region warm standby.
- We can add a clause for a "burst protection notice" where Redwood will proactively notify Novamed when cumulative burst minutes exceed 75% of daily allowance.

Attachment: Redwood_proposed_sla_clauses_v1.docx (docx)

Karthik
Principal, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Claire Donovan <claire@novamed.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: pilot SLA addendum for regional burst protection

Hi Claire / Procurement — forwarding Karthik's draft language. Commercial impact summary:

- The proposed 15% burst tolerance and 3 hours/day allowance can be accommodated within the pilot without a Dedicated sizing change for modest baselines (<= 2x baseline traffic). If you expect sustained bursts materially above that, we will need to increase baseline capacity which will change the Order Form.
- The grace window (30 minutes) is intended to reduce noisy credit events; it does not waive remediation obligations.
- Pricing delta for the addendum (pilot, 90 days): $6,500/month incremental for reserved buffer and monitoring/ops support (this is a bundled rate covering warm standby routing and prioritized on-call during pilot hours).

Requested next steps:
1) If procurement is OK with the pricing delta and evidence checklist, we'll insert the proposed clauses into the Order Form and provide a DocuSign-ready redline.
2) If you prefer a different credits cap or grace period, let us know and we can produce an alternative redline.

Attachment: OrderForm_Draft_ND-2027-0911.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Claire Donovan <claire@novamed.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pilot SLA addendum for regional burst protection

Thanks Michael / team — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from procurement/legal before we move to redlines:

- Evidence: the list you gave is fine, but procurement needs a concrete retention window for audit logs (we require 90 days of logs for pilot investigations). Can you confirm Redwood will retain the relevant audit/tracing logs for 90 days?
- Grace window: our clinical ops lead prefers a shorter failover grace window — 15 minutes — because the pilot routes clinically urgent requests during business hours. If you can support 15 minutes, we'll accept the rest as-is. Otherwise we need an operational runbook describing the failover mechanics and RTO targets.
- Credits cap: procurement is okay with the 15% monthly cap for a trial, but asks that the credits schedule be explicit for multi-region events (i.e., event-level vs. monthly aggregation).
- DocuSign timeline: can we get a redline by EOD Friday so our legal can turn around within 2 business days?

We can also provide a short example traffic spreadsheet if that helps validate the burst allowance calculation.

Attachments: sample_traffic_profile.csv (csv)

Best,
Claire

Claire — appreciate the clear feedback. Quick confirmations:

- Log retention: we can commit to 90 days of the audit/tracing artifacts you listed for the pilot. We'll include the retention clause in the addendum.
- Grace window: Karthik and I discussed — we can accept a 15-minute grace window for the pilot if Novamed agrees to a slightly reduced burst tolerance (12% for up to 2.5 hours/day) to balance operational risk. We'll put both options in the redline (15-min / 30-min) and highlight the tradeoffs.
- Credits: we'll make the schedule explicit for event-level credits and a monthly aggregation cap.
- DocuSign: Michael and I will produce a redline by EOD Friday and include a DocuSign-ready order form.

I'll follow up with the redline and a short operational runbook excerpt for the failover mechanics in the same package.

Mina
